paper_a.title: Greed is Good: Algorithmic Results for Sparse Approximation

metadata.description: Both papers attack the same underlying problem of recovering a sparse vector from an underdetermined linear system, but through substantially different theoretical machinery. Tropp analyzes a greedy algorithm (OMP) alongside Basis Pursuit using a deterministic coherence-based framework (Exact Recovery Condition, cumulative coherence) over a fixed dictionary, while Candes-Tao analyze the convex Basis Pursuit decoder for random Gaussian coding matrices via the Restricted Isometry Property and a dual-certificate construction. The two papers reach overlapping conclusions about exact ell_1 recovery from different angles, qualifying as competing frameworks (CF) for the same recovery question.

matches.explanation: Both formalize the sparsest-representation problem: Tropp's (D,m)-EXACT-SPARSE asks to recover the sparsest m-term representation of a signal known to be m-sparse over a dictionary; Candes-Tao's (P_0) is the ell_0-minimization version min ||d||_0 s.t. Fd = y. These are the same NP-hard combinatorial problem stated in equivalent dictionary-vs-matrix language.

Tropp's (D,m)-SPARSE asks for the best m-term approximation in ell_2; Candes-Tao's compressible-signal recovery problem reconstructs an alpha in F_s(B) from K linear measurements via ell_1. Both target approximate recovery of nonexactly-sparse signals, but the formulations differ (best-m-term ell_2 vs. compressible-class ell_2 error guarantee).

Tropp's Basis Pursuit algorithm (BP) solves min ||b||_1 s.t. sum_omega b_omega phi_omega = s — the exact convex relaxation that Candes-Tao formulate as (P_1) and implement as the ell_1 LP decoder AP114.1. Both papers cite Chen-Donoho-Saunders as the origin and recast as a linear program; the only difference is dictionary-vs-coding-matrix framing.

Both quantify how close columns of the measurement operator are to orthonormality. Tropp's coherence mu = max |<phi_i, phi_j>| measures pairwise inner products and yields per-pair bounds; Candes-Tao's restricted isometry constants delta_S measure singular-value deviation of every S-column submatrix. They play the same conceptual role (control of column dependencies) but coherence is a global pairwise scalar and RIP is a uniform sub-Grammian spectral bound — fundamentally different machinery.

Tropp's cumulative coherence mu_1(m) = max_{|Lambda|=m} max_{psi notin Lambda} sum |<psi, phi_lambda>| measures total inner-product budget between an outside atom and m chosen ones. Candes-Tao's restricted orthogonality theta_{S,S'} bounds |<F_T c, F_{T'} c'>| over disjoint supports. Both refine the pairwise notion (coherence / RIP) to control off-diagonal cross-terms between disjoint subsets, but mu_1 is L^1 in inner products while theta is L^2 / spectral.

Tropp's spark (least number of linearly dependent atoms) is the classical combinatorial sparsity-uniqueness invariant; Candes-Tao's Lemma 1.3 gives RIP-based uniqueness (delta_{2S} < 1 implies unique recovery from F_T c). Both establish sparse-representation uniqueness, with spark being a hard combinatorial quantity and delta_{2S} < 1 a quantitative spectral surrogate.

Both state the basic uniqueness theorem for sparse representations: Donoho-Elad/Gribonval-Nielsen via spark (m < spark(D)/2 iff unique), and Candes-Tao's Lemma 1.3 via RIP (delta_{2S} < 1 forces uniqueness). Same theorem under different sufficient conditions; in fact spark(D)/2 > m iff every 2m-column submatrix is full rank, which is exactly the qualitative content of delta_{2S} < 1.

Tropp's Lemma 2.3 gives a coherence-based singular-value lower bound: squared singular values of Phi_Lambda exceed 1 - mu_1(m-1). This is precisely the coherence-derived analogue of the RIP definition (1 - delta_S <= squared singular values <= 1 + delta_S). Tropp uses Gershgorin to derive what Candes-Tao take as a hypothesis on Gaussian matrices.

Both are the central exact-recovery theorem for Basis Pursuit. Tropp (TP113.7 + coherence-flavored CP113.2): BP recovers the sparsest representation under the Exact Recovery Condition max_psi ||Phi_opt^+ psi||_1 < 1, sharpened to coherence bound (2m-1)mu < 1 or mu_1(m) + mu_1(m-1) < 1. Candes-Tao Theorem 1.4: BP uniquely recovers c when delta_S + theta_S + theta_{S,2S} < 1. Same conclusion (BP exact recovery under sufficient near-orthogonality), but proved via dual-certificate norm bound vs. RIP/orthogonality sum.

Donoho-Huo (cited by Tropp as TP113.5) proved BP recovery for two-ONB dictionaries when m < (1 + 1/mu)/2 — a coherence-only sufficient condition. Candes-Tao TP114.1 generalizes far beyond two-ONB to arbitrary matrices satisfying the RIP/orthogonality bound. Same conclusion (BP recovers exact sparse representation), with Candes-Tao providing the modern framework that subsumes the Donoho-Huo regime.

Tropp's exact recovery theorem for OMP (the greedy algorithm) and its proof have no counterpart in Candes-Tao, who consider only the convex (BP) decoder. This is the central distinguishing contribution of Tropp's paper — analyzing the greedy algorithm under the same ERC that governs BP.
Converse for OMP (sharpness of ERC for greedy recovery) — paper-original to Tropp; Candes-Tao have no greedy converse since they analyze only BP.

Tropp's general (nonsparse) recovery results for OMP — the General Recovery Condition and the OMP-as-approximation-algorithm corollaries — are paper-original analyses of the greedy algorithm with no analogue in Candes-Tao's BP-only treatment.

Weak Orthogonal Matching Pursuit is the paper-original greedy algorithm in Tropp (Matching Pursuit AP113.1 and OMP AP113.2 are cited externals). Candes-Tao consider no greedy methods at all, so this has no counterpart on the Candes-Tao side.

Tropp's Theorem 3.5 expresses ERC via cumulative coherence (mu_1(m) + mu_1(m-1) < 1) — a coherence-language sufficient condition for ERC. Candes-Tao operate entirely in RIP language and have no cumulative-coherence analog; the closest spirit-match is the role of TP114.1's hypothesis delta_S + theta_S + theta_{S,2S} < 1, but the underlying objects (mu_1 vs theta) are sufficiently different that we treat this as paper-original.

Tropp's multi-ONB ERC results refine the coherence framework for L-orthonormal-basis dictionaries (Feuer-Nemirovsky-sharp two-ONB form, L-basis generalization). These are dictionary-structure-specific results outside the scope of Candes-Tao's random-matrix framework.

Composite parent-level proof match: both papers prove exact BP recovery by exhibiting that any nonoptimal candidate has strictly larger ell_1 norm. Tropp's PP113.4 splits into optimal/nonoptimal atoms and applies a strict ell_1 inequality (LP113.2) plus the operator inequality from ERC. Candes-Tao's PP114.5 (proof of TP114.1) constructs a dual certificate w via Lemma 2.2 (LP114.4), itself built iteratively (AP114.2/PP114.4) from Lemma 2.1 (LP114.3/PP114.3), then compares ||d||_1 to ||c||_1 via the dual vector. Same dual-certificate / strict-inequality strategy in spirit, but Tropp's argument is direct from the ERC bound while Candes-Tao require an iterative dual construction tailored to RIP+orthogonality.

Composite step-block match between the two papers' inner constructions. Tropp's PSP113.5-8 (proof of cumulative-coherence ERC bound) expand the pseudoinverse, bound by mu_1(m), Neumann-series the inverse using ||A||_{1,1} <= mu_1(m-1), then combine. Candes-Tao's PSP114.5-8 (proof of Lemma 2.2, the dual-certificate construction) initialize with Lemma 2.1, iteratively annihilate, sum the alternating series w = sum (-1)^{n-1} w_n using the contraction theta_{S,2S}/(1-delta_S) < 1, and conclude with cancellation/geometric-bound off T. Both are Neumann-style geometric-series constructions that depend on a contraction strictly less than 1 (mu_1(m-1) < 1 vs. theta_{S,2S}/(1-delta_S) < 1) — this is a genuine structural parallel of method despite operating in different norm contexts.
Tropp's proposition mu_1(m) <= m mu (and its trivial proof) is internal to the cumulative-coherence framework; no counterpart in Candes-Tao.
Tropp's measure-zero observation about exact m-sparse signals (Section IV motivation) is paper-specific framing; Candes-Tao do not state an analogous measure-theoretic lemma.

Tropp's foundational definitions of dictionary/atoms (unit-norm spanning collection in C^d) and m-term representation are dictionary-language preliminaries. Candes-Tao work directly in matrix-vector form (F, A) and never introduce a dictionary abstraction or a corresponding m-term representation definition.
Tropp's exact-recovery corollary for WOMP under ERC < alpha; Candes-Tao have no greedy or weak-greedy analogue.
Tropp's Gershgorin-disc proof of the singular-value lower bound (LP113.1) — a coherence-specific Gram-matrix argument with no counterpart in Candes-Tao's RIP framework.

Candes-Tao's proof of Lemma 1.3 (uniqueness from delta_{2S} < 1) is a short RIP-based contradiction argument. Tropp's spark-based uniqueness theorem TP113.1 is cited from Donoho-Elad without a proof in Tropp's paper, so there is no paired Tropp proof to align.
Candes-Tao's overarching error-correcting decoding problem (recover f from y = Af + e) is the coding-theoretic framing absent from Tropp, who works purely in dictionary/sparse-approximation language.

Candes-Tao's primal ell_1 decoding problem (P_1') min_g ||y - Ag||_1 is the decoder formulation tied to their coding setup; Tropp's BP is stated as an equality-constrained min ||b||_1 over dictionary coefficients with no analogue of the Af + e measurement model.
Lemma 1.2 (theta-delta relationship) and its proof are internal to the RIP/orthogonality framework; no counterpart in Tropp's coherence framework.
Candes-Tao's ell_1 decoding recovery theorem TP114.2 transfers TP114.1 to the Af + e coding setting via the annihilator F with FA = 0. Tropp has no decoding/error-correction theorem.

Random-matrix RIP analysis is paper-original to Candes-Tao: the Gaussian restricted isometry theorem, its corollary for Gaussian coding matrices, the underlying tail bound (Lemma 3.1) and its proof via Ledoux concentration plus Stirling union bound. Tropp's framework is entirely deterministic-coherence-based, with no random-matrix or concentration content.

Candes-Tao's compressible-signal reconstruction theorem (TP114.4) gives an ell_2 error bound on the order of (K/lambda)^{-(s-1/2)} for signals in F_s(B). Tropp's CP113.5/CP113.6 give an ell_2 approximation guarantee for OMP relative to the best m-term approximation, which is a different non-exact-recovery setting (greedy near-best vs. compressible-class min-max).
Compressible-signal class F_s(B) (decreasing rearrangement decay |alpha|_(k) <= B k^{-s}) is paper-specific to Candes-Tao's section 5; Tropp does not work with such a structured signal class.

Candes-Tao's framing equations — the sparse-error assumption, the FA = 0 annihilator reduction, and the LP reformulation — are setup machinery for the decoding problem that has no parallel in Tropp's pure dictionary setting.
